### **Job Description and Duties**

Under the close supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist performs a range of duties including lead responsibilities over seasonal and permanent staff performing eradication, detection trapping and survey activities, statewide research, detection trapping quality control, post quarantine inspections, outreach and logistics, and writing reports for agricultural programs for PD/EP. This involves interaction with federal, State, county, private agencies, and other stakeholder groups.

As an employee of the California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!

Join a passionate, collaborative team where your expertise directly shapes sustainable solutions for our planet's most precious resources, agricultural. We empower our environmental scientists with cutting-edge technology and the autonomy to spearhead meaningful, high-impact conservation with our pest detection or eradication projects. Here, your work goes beyond protecting agriculture—you will be actively building a cleaner, safer, and more resilient future for local communities.

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The CDFA does not participate in E-Verify for employment authorization purposes.

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The work settings vary. The settings could be permanent buildings or trailers leased or owned by the state or cooperating agencies or other locations. The employee may work in isolated locations and may work alone for extended periods. The duties of this position are primarily conducted outdoors and may be exposed to extreme temperatures and weather, uneven terrain, and various noise levels. The incumbent may work within an office/warehouse environment furnished with a variety of office equipment, which normally consists of desks, tables, chairs, filing cabinets, storage cabinets, filing bins, computers, computer peripherals, phones, photocopiers, and fax machines. Computer software used may include Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Access and Publisher.

The incumbent must be able to apply pesticides, haul loads of fruit and/or removed trees, perform survey work, and work well under extreme time constraints, exercise good judgment, determine priorities, make appropriate well-thought out decisions, allocate staff and resources to achieve maximum results, maintain focus under conditions of duress, and provide accurate assessment of rapidly changing situations (ex: multiple exotic pest detections requiring multiple operations).

The incumbent will be required to drive, exit and re-enter the work vehicle numerous times during the workday, must possess a valid CA drivers’ license and maintain a good standing driving record to operate a state motor vehicle safely and responsibly, be able to apply pesticides. The incumbent must be able to establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted during the course of work, cooperate with other staff members and leads in completing assigned work, communicate effectively verbally and in writing, with other agencies and the public, and be able to meet required deadlines.

The incumbent will be required to travel by State or rental vehicle to perform field active or other public transportation systems to various locations throughout the state. Must be legally able to rent a car. May work various shifts (pre-dawn and after 6:00 pm), weekends, overtime, and possibly a split shift.

The incumbent may also be required to travel on short notice that requires several continuous nights in length or work extended hours and days at any given time in the month including weekends, overtime, and holidays.

Travel is essential and the incumbent will travel to locations throughout the state to attend meetings or training related to pest detection, survey, and treatment activities and to assist other offices with detection and treatment efforts are required.

The incumbent must have a valid California driver’s license and have a safe driving record as documented by the Department of Motor Vehicles. (A safe driving record is one free from convictions in the past two years for repeated moving violations, or a single serious violation, such as drunk driving or reckless driving).

This position may/may not be eligible for telework. The amount of telework is at the discretion of the CDFA and based on the current telework policy. While the CDFA supports telework where possible, in-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. Employees are expected to be able to report to their worksite with minimal notification if an urgent need arises, as determined by the Department.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
This position plays an important role in the implementation of DPR’s statewide pesticide registration program that is responsible for evaluating the impact of proposed pesticide products on human health and the environment. Working under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), the Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) performs a range of duties including but not limited to:

* Independently researches, analyzes, and develops proposed environmental permitting packages on the Department’s proposed registration decisions, including public reports, consistent with the program’s functional equivalency status under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA). Evaluates, analyzes, interprets, and summarizes complex scientific data/evaluations of data in the scientific disciplines of toxicology, ecotoxicology, chemistry, environmental fate, microbiology, air, and water supporting the registration or amendment of pesticide products to protect the state’s natural resources and public health, and carries out the goals and objectives of the program. Assesses chemical and non-chemical alternative pest control methods relative to their potential for human health and environmental impacts using federal and state guidelines and scientific standards. Researches, analyzes, and evaluates pest management practices and pesticide use data to support assessments of pest management alternatives and cumulative impacts.

* Analyzes and responds to public comments raising significant adverse environmental points on proposed registration decisions. Informs the pesticide manufacturer of the comment, analyzes pesticide manufacturer’s response, and drafts written responses to complex public comments. Ensures responses to all written comments meet CEQA requirements for public postings of the Department’s final registration decisions.

* Performs critical and complex pest management analysis, assessment, research, and investigations to determine similarity of new and amended pesticide product formulations and compares intended uses to previously approved pesticide products. Assesses percentage and composition of chemicals, pest organisms (including insects, plants, and microbes), methods of pesticide applications, and application rates on pesticide labels.

The duties of this position are performed indoors in a high-rise building. The candidate must possess the ability to:

Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. ### **Job Description and Duties**

Join the Environmental Monitoring Program (EMP) as an estuarine scientist! Our long-term monitoring program collects data on water quality and biological (phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate) communities in the San Francisco Bay-Delta estuary to ensure regulatory compliance with Water Right Decision 1641 (D-1641). In this role, the incumbent will coordinate and serve as crew lead on monthly monitoring surveys aboard research vessels and by vehicle, making sure sampling is done safely and follows standard operating procedures (SOPs). The incumbent will maintain, calibrate, and install field equipment such as YSI EXO2 water quality sondes, and perform basic laboratory analyses. The incumbent will review and provide feedback on scientific and technical documents and coordinate with internal and external collaborators and stakeholders to execute special studies on emerging environmental issues in the Bay-Delta.

If you are passionate about water quality, regulatory compliance, large-scale infrastructure programs, and building efficient operational processes, we encourage you to apply!

Job Description

Project Name:
Hazard Assessment Program

Project Description:

Under the State of California’s new cross-connection control regulations, the SFPUC must review all service connections (~180,000+) to properties in San Francisco, as well as the eight other water systems under SFPUC’s control, to evaluate potential hazards to the public drinking water distribution system arising from activities on user premises. In addition, the new regulations require the installation of backflow prevention assemblies on about 4,200 fire service connections. SFPUC has submitted a plan to the State Water Resources Control Board with deadlines for completing hazard assessments by 2049, ensuring backflow prevention assemblies on all dedicated fire services by 2044.

Position Summary

Are you a technical professional looking to make a direct impact on public health and water safety on a massive scale? We are seeking a dynamic Utility Specialist to serve as the Technical Program Coordinator for our Water Quality Cross Connection Control (CCC) Program under the direction of the Hazard Assessments Program Manager.

In this vital role, you will contribute to the implementation of SFPUC Cross-Connection Control Program inline with new regulatory requirements established by the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) through the Cross Connection Control Policy Handbook (CCCPH).

You will help shape a high-profile, multi-decade program by developing tracking systems, operational processes, coordinating complex field logistics, and partnering with internal teams, contractors, and external stakeholders across multiple program areas including Hazard Assessments, Fire services upgrades and Regional Compliance.

Work Location:
1657 Rollins Road, Burlingame, CA, 94010

Schedule:
Full-time, Monday – Friday

This position requires a valid driver’s license.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Implementation & Compliance: Develop and implement coordination protocols, workflows, and documentation processes for the CCC Program in compliance with SWRCB CCCPH requirements.
Systems & Data Management: Establish tracking systems, dashboards, and reporting templates to monitor inspections, costs, schedules, and compliance metrics.
Research & Analysis: Conduct research using internal databases, GIS systems, spreadsheets, field reports, and photos to compile baseline data on service connection characteristics and assess cross-connection hazards.
Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinate daily program activities with field staff, contractors, customers, and other City departments, serving as a liaison to ensure smooth communication, scheduling, and execution.
Contractor & Consultant Oversight: Coordinate with contractors and consultants to ensure field activities align with approved scopes of work, schedules, and Cross Connection Control program requirements.
Reporting & Continuous Improvement: Prepare program reports, dashboards, and documentation for Program Manager review, highlighting trends, risks, and lessons learned while developing procedures, reference materials, and recommendations to improve program effectiveness.
Field Engagement: Conduct field coordination and site visits (as needed) to support hazard assessments, inspection activities, and validation of program data.
Technical Support: Provide technical support for Hazard Assessment Program initiatives, including compliance studies, analytical tasks, and administrative support. Performs other project-related duties as assigned.

What We’re Looking For (Desirable Qualifications)

We are seeking analytical, highly organized professionals who bring technical expertise and strong stakeholder management skills to our team. Ideal candidates possess:

Technical or Scientific Degree: A baccalaureate degree in a technical or scientific field, such as Civil, Environmental, Mechanical, or Chemical Engineering, Environmental Science, Physical Science, or a closely related discipline.
Compliance & Program Management Experience: Demonstrated experience coordinating or managing compliance, regulatory, technical, or project/program-related work within a water utility, similar utility environment, public agency, or closely related regulatory setting.
Project Coordination Mastery: Strong organizational and project coordination skills, including managing multiple priorities, tracking activities, monitoring progress, and maintaining accurate records .
Stakeholder Engagement: Proven experience communicating and working collaboratively with diverse stakeholders, including field staff, contractors, regulators and customers.
Technical & Analytical Acumen: Ability to conduct regulatory research, analyze technical and operational information, and support the development and implementation of policies, procedures and program improvements .
Data Management: Proficiency using advanced Excel functions (e.g., formulas, pivot tables, data validation, lookups) to manage datasets, track program performance, and support regulatory reporting.
Water Systems Knowledge: Basic knowledge of water service and distribution systems, cross -connections, backflow prevention principles (backpressure and backsiphonage) and applicable water quality requirements.
Regulatory Familiarity: Familiarity with Federal, State, and local laws, codes, and regulations applicable to drinking water, water distribution systems.

Please note, candidates must meet the minimum qualifications
in order to be considered for desirable qualifications. For more information on this position's minimum qualifications, see section below.

Qualifications

Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university preferably with major coursework in Law, Engineering, Environmental Studies, Natural Resources, Computer Science, Business Administration, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, or other field related to the utility business; AND

Experience:

Four years of verifiable journey-level work experience in one or more of the following areas: planning, scheduling, cost estimating and resource projecting for mid to large scale projects; water supply/infrastructure management and planning; power operations planning and scheduling; analysis, interpretation and application of utility contracts and regulations in either water, power (electric and/or natural gas), telecommunications, or a wastewater/clean water program; utility market and environmental analysis and planning; power supply and transmission rates and contracts; generation, transmission or distribution planning and design; or long-term utility systems planning.

The WBG Chief Risk Officer (CRO) Vice Presidency is the core unit responsible for Group-wide institutional risk oversight, including establishment and monitoring adherence to risk policies and guidelines and risk assessment and reporting to the Board and executive management. Its mission is to enable and support the WBG to achieve its goals in a financially sustainable manner. The VPU assists management with identifying and managing Group-wide cross-cutting risks, enhancing risk response decisions, reducing financial and operational surprises and losses, seizing opportunities and improving deployment of capital. The WBG CRO Vice Presidency includes the IBRD/IDA, IFC, and MIGA risk teams and covers a wide range of financial and non-financial risks.

To enhance accountability and credibility, the World Bank Group (WBG) has established an independent second line of environmental and social risk oversight within its Chief Risk Officer (CRO) function called CROES. While operational teams at the World Bank, IFC, and MIGA are responsible for designing and implementing projects in accordance with E&S policies, the newly formed E&S Risk Department—led by the WBG Global Director for Environment and Social Risk—oversees, monitors, and evaluates E&S risk and performance.

CROES seeks a seasoned, dynamic, and motivated Senior Environmental or Social Specialist with strong technical judgment and substantial experience in social risk management. The selected candidate will support independent second-line oversight of operations and portfolios across the World Bank Group, with balanced thematic coverage of environmental and social aspects, such as pollution prevention, labor and working conditions; land acquisition, biodiversity conservation, resettlement and livelihood restoration; stakeholder engagement and grievance mechanisms. The role will identify project-level and systemic social and environmental risks, assess the adequacy of mitigation and implementation arrangements, and provide clear advice to CROES management and senior decision-makers.

Independent E&S Risk Oversight

Assess the adequacy of E&S risk identification, assessment, mitigation measures, monitoring arrangements, and escalation pathways proposed by operational teams, while maintaining independence from first-line responsibilities.
Provide independent technical opinions on E&S risk categorization, application of relevant E&S policies and standards, adequacy of mitigation measures, institutional capacity, and implementation readiness.
Review project documentation, E&S assessments and management plans, stakeholder engagement arrangements, advisory products, and relevant legal commitments from an independent E&S risk perspective.

Lead or support quality assurance reviews of selected operations, assessing the quality of E&S due diligence, management of stakeholder impacts, feasibility of mitigation measures, and capacity to meet applicable E&S requirements.

Portfolio Monitoring and Analytics

Lead portfolio-level monitoring and assessment of E&S risks and performance across sectors, regions, and WBG institutions.
Develop and maintain an E&S Risk Watch List highlighting projects with elevated environmental, social, stakeholder, compliance, implementation, reputational, or development outcome risks.
Conduct thematic and sector-specific portfolio reviews to identify systemic E&S risk trends, recurring implementation challenges, and emerging risk patterns.
Analyze E&S risk events and lessons learned to strengthen institutional risk practices and contribute to enterprise-level reporting and integrated risk dashboards for senior management and governance committees.
Recommend improvements to E&S risk management practices based on portfolio experience, independent assessments, and international good practices.
Monitor E&S risks in projects subject to accountability mechanism reviews, CAO or Inspection Panel processes, integrity investigations, significant stakeholder complaints, disputes, or public controversy.
Advise on risk implications of complaints, disputes, compliance findings, and corporate management responses.
Coordinate with operational teams, regional ESG specialists, and other relevant functions to assess the implications of E&S issues for implementation, development outcomes, and WBG reputation.

Delineation of wetlands using the appropriate regional supplements to the USACE Wetland Delineation Manual

Completion of biological assessments such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat field surveys

Assistance with preparation of USACE Section 404 permit applications
Assistance with preparation of State 401 Water Quality Certification applications (including Georgia EPD state waters buffer variances)
Assistance with preparation of NPDES construction stormwater permit applications
Completion of E&SC inspections on active construction sites
Environmental sampling while following appropriate sample integrity and chain-of-custody procedures
Sample coordination with appropriate laboratory for sample analysis
Site visits to document other environmental compliance and associated reporting

BS degree in natural resources, ecology, environmental science, fisheries, wildlife biology, chemistry, geology, environmental engineering, or related discipline
MS degree is preferred, but not required

Knowledge of eastern United States flora and fauna, especially wetland and riparian flora

OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER certification is preferred, but not required
Ability to work long, physically demanding hours in a variety of weather conditions in remote locations
Ability to traverse uneven terrain and carry field equipment (up to 40 lbs)
Advanced written and verbal communication skills
